name: dense_city_hwrt_high
title: Dense City Blocks with Nanite, NextGI High: the G5-1 whole frame and its feature totals (GN-2, GN-11; GN-13's Dense City half)

lines.name: Dense City + NextGI High, whole frame
lines.reason: The GodotNext side is every timed pass of the frame, against UE's whole-frame GPU time. GodotNext's virtual shadow maps are not built yet (the engine has no shadow_method setting), so its side renders the scene's shadows on the shadow atlas (the sun's 4 directional splits and the street lights' shadow faces) while UE renders Virtual Shadow Maps, the comparison project's shadow method (r.Shadow.Virtual.Enable, which the report checks from each run's echo); the line is not like for like until GodotNext's virtual shadow maps land. UE also runs distance-field shadows (GPU/DistanceFieldShadows is busy in these captures). The settings record's far-shadow row says they are on by default for directional lights, shadow what lies beyond the dynamic shadow distance and work in tandem with Virtual Shadow Maps; GodotNext has not built them yet. UE takes the hardware tier from r.Lumen.HardwareRayTracing 1, set per launch as the lead accepted on 2026-11-16, because the shared comparison project keeps Use Hardware Ray Tracing when available off.

lines.name: G5-1 NextGI total against Lumen, hardware tier, High
lines.reason: The GodotNext group is the NextGI frame block (nextgi_* without the closing marker's column and line 1b), as GS-9's on the kitbash set; like every hardware-tier NextGI total it also takes skinned_refit_ms, line 1a's column without the prefix, on frames with skinned BLAS work (the city has none). The UE group takes every pass the captures show doing that work, by the lead's column rule (2026-11-16; plan §23.5 states it since v3.9.7, and the settings record now lists the observed columns): for line 1a, GPU/RayTracingScene, the TLAS build (the settings record's skinned refit row names it from Epic's ray tracing performance guide), and no GPU/RayTracingDynamicGeometry, which this capture of a city without skinned meshes lacks; the Lumen scene update, GPU/LumenSceneUpdate and GPU/UpdateLumenSceneBuffers; and the three stat gpu passes the settings record names for the Lumen total. Two busy columns stay out until the lead decides which GodotNext line, if any, does their work: GPU/NaniteRayTracing, busy in every hardware-tier capture and absent on the software tier, and GPU/DistanceFields, busy in every capture on both tiers and in the sets without Lumen. NextGI's hardware tier traces the kit's fixed RT proxies (rt_max_error 2 cm). Lumen's hardware ray tracing at r.RayTracing.Nanite.Mode 0 (the default, which each run's echo confirms) traces each Nanite mesh's fallback mesh, or its ray tracing proxy when the project setting Generate Ray Tracing Proxies is on, which the settings record leaves unconfirmed for 5.9; the UE import keeps the fallback at its import default, 251 to 1,005 triangles per kit mesh in its readback. Whether UE traces a comparable density waits for the lead. UE takes the hardware tier from r.Lumen.HardwareRayTracing 1, set per launch as the lead accepted on 2026-11-16, because the shared comparison project keeps Use Hardware Ray Tracing when available off.

lines.name: NextGeo cull + Hi-Z + visibility against Nanite raster and cull (G5-1 cull line; GN-2's Dense City line)
lines.reason: Provisional groups on both sides (plan §23.5 names neither column). GodotNext: the main view's NextGeo passes from the instance cull through the second raster pass, each column running from its timestamp to the next one (the resolve classification starts after the second raster pass). UE: GPU/NaniteVisBuffer, the Nanite column whose name says it draws the visibility buffer, the raster and cull of the main view in these captures; the HZB the frame builds afterwards is a separate column (GPU/HZB), and Nanite's virtual shadow map raster runs inside GPU/ShadowDepths. Whether UE's group takes the HZB as GodotNext's takes its Hi-Z waits for the lead; the settings record names the final columns. The UE import leaves the ground plane (2 triangles, without NextGeo virtual geometry in the export) off Nanite, as GodotNext draws it outside NextGeo, so neither side's group holds the ground. Plan §23.4 (v3.9.7) says port meshes get Nanite in UE even where the GodotNext content leaves NextGeo off; whether that covers the ground of a scene whose other meshes are NextGeo waits for the lead.

lines.name: NextGeo resolve, Stage A + Stage B, against Nanite shading (G5-1 resolve line; GN-11 Stage A+B)
lines.reason: Provisional groups on both sides (plan §23.5 names neither column). GodotNext: the Stage A and Stage B resolve columns, without the resolve classification (binning, report-only line N3); the compute shading bins (#158) are not built, so the resolve draws 8x8 tile quads per material bucket. UE: GPU/NaniteBasePass, Nanite's material shading in these captures. The settings record names the final columns. The UE import leaves the ground plane (2 triangles, without NextGeo virtual geometry in the export) off Nanite, as GodotNext draws it outside NextGeo, so neither side's group holds the ground. Plan §23.4 (v3.9.7) says port meshes get Nanite in UE even where the GodotNext content leaves NextGeo off; whether that covers the ground of a scene whose other meshes are NextGeo waits for the lead.

lines.name: G5-1 VSM total against Virtual Shadow Maps
lines.reason: No GodotNext group (V1 to V5). GodotNext's virtual shadow maps are not built yet (the engine has no shadow_method setting), so its side renders the scene's shadows on the shadow atlas (the sun's 4 directional splits and the street lights' shadow faces) while UE renders Virtual Shadow Maps, the comparison project's shadow method (r.Shadow.Virtual.Enable, which the report checks from each run's echo); the line is not like for like until GodotNext's virtual shadow maps land. UE: the settings record's two stat gpu buckets, GPU/ShadowDepths and GPU/ShadowProjection in these captures, where every light of the scene renders Virtual Shadow Maps; the sun's distance-field shadows (GPU/DistanceFieldShadows) stay out, as the settings record's far-shadow row has no timing stat. The CSV category VSM the settings record names is not in the default capture, and no public page says whether GPU/Lights counts the projection again; the group is provisional.

lines.name: Render-thread CPU, Dense City (GN-13 adds Foliage Field)
lines.reason: GN-13 judges the render-thread time of Dense City and Foliage Field together (plan §21.4.3); this set records the Dense City half (#234's foliage_field set holds the other), and the sum across the two sets is not defined in the harness yet. The GodotNext render-thread column group is not defined yet either.
